nodes.label: Claude Code plugin scaffolding
nodes.summary: Guides creating and organizing a Claude Code plugin: directory layout, manifest, component placement, and troubleshooting why a component fails to load.

nodes.label: Convention-based auto-discovery
nodes.summary: Components are found by living in conventional directories with conventional filenames rather than being enumerated in config. Custom manifest paths supplement, never replace, the defaults.

nodes.label: Manifest as declared identity
nodes.summary: plugin.json at .claude-plugin/ carries the kebab-case name, semver version, metadata, and optional component paths. Name and path-shape errors are the common validation failures.

nodes.label: Install-location-independent paths
nodes.summary: Intra-package references must go through an environment root variable (${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}) because the install location varies by method and OS. Hardcoded absolute or cwd-relative paths break.

nodes.label: Progressive disclosure of skill content
nodes.summary: A lean SKILL.md carries core concepts; references/ and examples/ hold detail that loads only when the task needs it. Keeps context cost proportional to the task.

nodes.label: Shared component library over duplication
nodes.summary: Cross-cutting assets live in one shared place (lib/, assets/, a shared stylesheet, a reused ext-apps bundle) and every consumer links to it rather than inlining a copy.

nodes.label: Start flat, restructure on growth
nodes.summary: Begin with the simplest flat layout and only move to categorized or hierarchical organization when component count justifies it. Deep nesting costs discovery time.

nodes.label: Build an MCP app with UI widgets
nodes.summary: Adds interactive UI resources on top of a plain MCP server so tools render forms, pickers, dashboards, and confirmations inline in chat, in Claude and other apps-surface hosts.

nodes.label: Tool returns data, resource serves UI
nodes.summary: A widget-enabled tool registers twice: the tool declares _meta.ui.resourceUri and returns plain text/JSON, while a separately registered ui:// resource serves the HTML the host renders in an iframe.

nodes.label: Graceful degradation to plain text
nodes.summary: Because the tool handler already returns meaningful data, hosts without the apps surface simply ignore _meta.ui and Claude reads the data directly. UI is additive, never load-bearing.

nodes.label: Iframe sandbox and CSP restrictions
nodes.summary: Widgets run in a locked-down iframe: no CDN script fetches, no window.open, no arbitrary network origins, no reliable remote images. Violations fail silently as a blank rectangle.

nodes.label: Build-time bundle inlining
nodes.summary: The ext-apps browser build is read at startup, its ESM export statement rewritten to a globalThis assignment, and substituted into a placeholder in the widget HTML so no CDN fetch is needed.

nodes.label: Silent blank widget
nodes.summary: The dominant MCP-app failure: the widget renders as an empty rectangle with no error in the host console, because a CSP violation surfaced only in the iframe's own devtools.

nodes.label: Persistent widget-host-server messaging
nodes.summary: The App class keeps a live bidirectional channel: ontoolresult/ontoolinput inbound, sendMessage and updateModelContext outbound to the conversation, callServerTool straight to the server, openLink for navigation.

nodes.label: Prefer the cheapest mechanism that works
nodes.summary: Route to the simplest sufficient tool: elicitation before a custom widget, plain text before UI, built-in tool before CLI fallback, non-AI script before an AI step.

nodes.label: One tool, one focused widget
nodes.summary: Keep each widget small and single-purpose rather than building a sub-app in the iframe. Fork layout by item count inside one tool instead of multiplying tools.

nodes.label: Watch a video
nodes.summary: Gives the agent video input: yt-dlp downloads the source, ffmpeg extracts auto-scaled frames, captions or Whisper supply a timestamped transcript, and the agent Reads each frame to answer grounded in both streams.

nodes.label: Silent setup preflight
nodes.summary: A fast --check runs before every invocation, emitting nothing on success and returning typed exit codes that map to an idempotent installer or a key prompt. Never announce success to the user.

nodes.label: External binary dependency
nodes.summary: Capability gated on locally installed executables and API keys (yt-dlp, ffmpeg/ffprobe, the gws CLI, the codex CLI, OPENAI_API_KEY). Absence is a preflight failure, not a runtime surprise.

nodes.label: Duration-scaled token budgeting
nodes.summary: Frame count and fps scale inversely with video duration under hard caps (2 fps, 100 frames), with a denser focused mode for a named range, so image tokens stay bounded.

nodes.label: Graded fallback chain
nodes.summary: Try the free/preferred path first and fall back only on failure: native captions before Whisper, Groq before OpenAI, built-in image_gen before the CLI model path.

nodes.label: Never downgrade silently
nodes.summary: Switching to a weaker model or path requires explicit user confirmation, and a failed run must be surfaced rather than blindly retried.

nodes.label: Generate or edit raster images
nodes.summary: Codex-side skill producing bitmap assets (photos, illustrations, mockups, cutouts) via the built-in image_gen tool by default, with a CLI/API fallback for true native transparency.

nodes.label: Teach a topic over multiple sessions
nodes.summary: Turns the working directory into a stateful teaching workspace producing self-contained HTML lessons, reference sheets, and a growing record of what the learner knows.

nodes.label: Mission grounds every decision
nodes.summary: A short concrete statement of why the user wants this, with success criteria and out-of-scope bounds. Every teaching choice traces back to it; vagueness gets interviewed out before anything is written.

nodes.label: Numbered decision-record ledger
nodes.summary: Append-only sequentially numbered records that capture non-obvious insight and get superseded rather than deleted, so a later session inherits what was settled. Used for learning records and ADRs alike.

nodes.label: Opinionated controlled vocabulary
nodes.summary: A glossary that picks one preferred term per concept, lists aliases to avoid, uses its own terms inside definitions, and is adhered to everywhere downstream.

nodes.label: Ground in trusted sources, not parametric memory
nodes.summary: Knowledge must come from a curated, annotated set of high-trust resources with citations; never trust the model's own recall. Gaps are surfaced explicitly to drive further search.

nodes.label: Desirable difficulty for storage strength
nodes.summary: Design for long-term retention over in-the-moment fluency using retrieval practice, spacing, and interleaving, and keep each lesson inside the learner's zone of proximal development.

nodes.label: Author JSON Canvas files
nodes.summary: Creates and edits .canvas files (nodes, edges, groups) per the JSON Canvas 1.0 spec for mind maps and flowcharts in Obsidian.

nodes.label: Post-write referential integrity check
nodes.summary: Every canvas mutation ends with re-parsing the JSON and confirming ID uniqueness plus that every fromNode/toNode resolves to an existing node.

nodes.label: Adversarial cross-model plan review
nodes.summary: Claude drafts a plan into PLAN.md and a read-only Codex session critiques it round after round, returning APPROVED or REVISE, until convergence or a round cap. No code is written during the loop.

nodes.label: Adversarial verification before shipping
nodes.summary: A skeptical second reviewer, ideally a different model or a fresh subagent, must try to break the artifact before it is built or merged. Agreeableness is the failure mode being designed against.

nodes.label: Read-only critic sandbox
nodes.summary: The critic can read the repo but must never write. The resume subcommand rejects -s, so read-only has to be forced via -c sandbox_mode, or config defaults could grant full write access mid-loop.

nodes.label: Bounded loop with an explicit cap
nodes.summary: Iteration always terminates at MAX_ROUNDS. Hitting the cap without approval is a legitimate flagged-disagreement outcome, never dressed up as convergence.

nodes.label: Resume the same session across rounds
nodes.summary: Capture the thread_id on round one and resume it thereafter so the critic remembers earlier critiques. Falling back to a fresh exec re-reads the repo and loses everything settled.

nodes.label: Re-assertion guard and finding triage
nodes.summary: Sort each finding into technical, product-decision, or already-rejected. A repeat finding without new evidence is logged as held; a product question goes straight to the human instead of burning a round.

nodes.label: Explicit human approval gate
nodes.summary: Named checkpoints where the human, not the model, decides: kickoff and final sign-off before code, gate approvals in a staged build, choosing merge versus PR, authorizing a fallback path.

nodes.label: Append-only argument transcript
nodes.summary: PLAN-REVIEW-LOG.md records every round's critique plus what was changed, what was rejected, and why. Described as the most valuable artifact of the run.

nodes.label: PLAN.md as the interchange artifact
nodes.summary: A structured plan document (goal, approach, contestable decisions, risks, out of scope) that models communicate through and that later becomes the frozen spec handed to an implementer.

nodes.label: Write an implementation plan
nodes.summary: Turns a spec into a dated plan document of bite-sized, independently testable tasks written for an engineer with zero codebase context, preceded by an explicit file-structure decomposition.

nodes.label: Task right-sizing around a review gate
nodes.summary: A task is the smallest unit carrying its own test cycle and worth a fresh reviewer's gate. Split only where a reviewer could reject one task while approving its neighbor; fold setup into the task that needs it.

nodes.label: Reviewer calibration against nitpicking
nodes.summary: A dispatched reviewer flags only issues that would cause real implementation problems (missing requirements, contradictions, placeholders, unactionable tasks) and approves past stylistic preferences.

nodes.label: Finish a development branch
nodes.summary: Verifies the test suite, detects whether the workspace is a normal repo or a worktree, determines the base branch, then presents merge/PR/cleanup options and executes the choice.

nodes.label: Green tests as a hard precondition
nodes.summary: Integration options are not even presented until the project's test suite passes. Failing tests stop the workflow rather than being noted and worked around.

nodes.label: Weekly automation level-up
nodes.summary: A weekly 3Ms interview (Mindset to find a candidate, Method to scope it, Machine to build it) that ends in exactly one shipped automation artifact for the EA workspace.

nodes.label: Eliminate before automating
nodes.summary: First ask what breaks if the task simply stops. If nothing breaks, log the win and exit; automating waste is worse than leaving it manual. Delegate to a person when the process is too variable.

nodes.label: Lowest autonomy level that works
nodes.summary: Default to the least autonomous option and require explicit choice to go higher. Anything a student or prospect reads is drafts-with-human-review minimum, never auto-sent.

nodes.label: Save-to-both catalog and activation
nodes.summary: Every new skill is written to both the activated project .claude/skills/ path and the DB catalog, project-scoped, with a Codex twin mirrored to .agents/skills/ when applicable.

nodes.label: Skill router / which-flow-fits
nodes.summary: ask-matt is a router over the user-invoked skills, laying out the main idea-to-ship flow, its on-ramps, codebase-health upkeep, and how to cross session boundaries.

nodes.label: Context-window hygiene and handoff
nodes.summary: Keep one phase inside one unbroken window while the model is still in its smart zone; when it fills, hand off to a fresh session via a written file rather than pushing on degraded.

nodes.label: Cross-runtime skill parity baseline
nodes.summary: PARITY.md declares every deliberately single-runtime skill with a justification, so check-skills.py fails only on undeclared drift. Catalog parity is explicitly distinct from activation.

nodes.label: Declared asymmetry, not silent drift
nodes.summary: A one-runtime skill is legitimate only when written down with a reason in the same commit. An undeclared gap is drift and must be either ported or declared; a list without reasons is a snapshot, not a decision.

nodes.label: Cross-model orchestration from the other runtime
nodes.summary: Skills that drive Codex must live only on the Claude side; giving them to Codex would mean Codex driving Codex, defeating the cross-model check that is their whole purpose.

nodes.label: Build an LSAT U bootcamp
nodes.summary: Clones the Intro to LR build end to end for a new topic: interview, content intake and tiering, inspection report, then a gated repo-native multi-session build until a parity audit passes.

nodes.label: Gated multi-session build with a checkpoint ledger
nodes.summary: Work advances through numbered gates, each requiring human approval; state persists in a vault build page with a gate ledger so a fresh session resumes at the current gate and never redoes an approved one.

nodes.label: Clone the reference implementation exactly
nodes.summary: The existing shipped build is the template, not a doc. Reuse its components, tokens, and chrome unchanged; deviations must be argued and approved at a gate.

nodes.label: No silently invented domain content
nodes.summary: Content comes from the author's own files; gaps are flagged for his decision rather than filled in. Missing reviewed content counts as a build failure, not something to paper over.

nodes.label: Fan-out deep research
nodes.summary: Reads an outline.yaml, skips already-completed items for resumability, and launches parallel background agents that each emit a schema-validated JSON record per research item.

nodes.label: Resumable batched agent fan-out
nodes.summary: Check the output directory for completed artifacts and skip them, then dispatch remaining work in approved batches of parallel agents with output suppressed.

nodes.label: Schema-validated structured output
nodes.summary: Each agent writes JSON against a field-definition file, marks uncertain values explicitly, and is not done until a validation script confirms complete field coverage.

nodes.label: Google Workspace access via the gws CLI
nodes.summary: A generated family of thin skills wrapping the gws CLI across Gmail, Sheets, Meet, Keep, and Workspace events, each documenting one command's flags and examples.

nodes.label: Shared prerequisite doc for auth and security
nodes.summary: Every gws skill defers auth, global flags, and security rules to one gws-shared page rather than repeating them, and points at gws generate-skills if it is missing.

nodes.label: Dry-run and draft modes on outbound actions
nodes.summary: Send-shaped commands expose --dry-run to show the request without executing and --draft to save instead of send, giving a rehearsal path before any irreversible outbound action.

nodes.label: Unread inbox triage listing
nodes.summary: Summarizes unread mail as sender/subject/date with a configurable max, arbitrary Gmail search query, and JSON output for downstream processing.

nodes.label: Send or reply to mail
nodes.summary: Sends new mail or reply-alls to an existing thread with automatic threading, sharing the same flag surface for recipients, attachments, HTML, alias sender, dry-run, and draft.

nodes.label: Edit and restructure an article
nodes.summary: Divides a draft into sections, confirms the section plan with the user, then rewrites each for clarity and flow under a tight paragraph-length constraint.

nodes.label: Dependency-ordered exposition
nodes.summary: Treat information as a directed acyclic graph: order sections so each piece is introduced only after everything it depends on. Mirrors teaching the knowledge a skill needs before practicing it.

nodes.label: User-invocation-only skills
nodes.summary: Some skills set disable-model-invocation so they never auto-trigger from context and run only when the user explicitly asks, protecting stateful or opinionated workflows from accidental starts.

nodes.label: Announce the skill at start
nodes.summary: Several build-side skills open by stating which skill is running, making the workflow legible to the user. Contrasts with the silent-on-success preflight convention.
